problem: Existing action-conditioned world models (NWM, IRASim, Ctrl-World, GrndCtrl) are domain-specific, use bespoke architectures that cannot exploit Internet-scale video diffusion priors, or use conditioning (global or cross-attention) that gives imprecise control or ignores temporal latent compression. Appearance metrics (LPIPS, DreamSim, FVD) also do not measure whether predicted futures actually follow the actions.
motivation: Action-labelled egocentric data is expensive, especially for complex embodiments like humanoids, while passive Internet video is abundant. A recipe that turns any pretrained video diffusion model into a controllable world model with little action data would scale across embodiments and environments and transfer to out-of-distribution scenes.
key_idea: Inject temporally downsampled action embeddings into the diffusion timestep-modulation pathway (added to the replicated timestep embedding) of any pretrained image-to-video diffusion model, which turns it into an action-conditioned world model without changing its architecture.
insight: Adding actions through the timestep pathway, aligned to the latent temporal resolution, gives more precise control and keeps pretrained priors better than the alternatives. Global conditioning lowers SCS by 44.8% and chunking by 12% on humanoid navigation, and cross-attention conditioning gets 23.6% lower SCS and worse perceptual metrics on OOD RECON. Pretraining matters: SVD fine-tuned beats SVD from scratch on 25-DoF humanoid navigation. Temporal compression (k=4) improves visual fidelity but degrades long-horizon action following relative to SVD (k=1).
method: Action Projection: lightweight MLPs embed each D-dim action (3-DoF (dx,dy,dphi) or 25-DoF humanoid joints) into d-dim vectors; 1D convs downsample to T/k for temporally compressed VAEs (k=4 for Cosmos/Wan).

Timestep-pathway injection: replicate the denoising timestep embedding along the compressed time axis and add the action embedding, then feed the sum to each block's scale/shift/gate projection F_i. No new layers are added inside the backbone.
Initial state embedding: for humanoids, where many body parts are out of view, add an embedding Z_s of the initial joint state to resolve ambiguity.

Fine-tuning: uses the base model's original objective (denoising or flow matching) on RECON+SCAND+TartanDrive (3-DoF) and 1X humanoid data; the action module's learning rate is 10x that of the base weights. Instantiated on SVD, Cosmos-Predict2-2B, and Wan2.1-14B.

Structural Consistency Score (SCS): AllTracker trims frames with no overlap with the first frame; SAM2 (or SAM3 for the automatic version) tracks passive structures/robot parts in GT and generated videos; SCS is the mean mask IoU over objects and frames.
Planning: goal-conditioned CEM, following NWM. Candidates are rolled out in EgoWM and scored by perceptual similarity between the predicted final frame and the goal image.

setting.backbone: SVD, Cosmos-Predict2-2B, Wan2.1-14B video diffusion models (fine-tuned) with action projection modules
setting.training_data: Pretrained Internet video diffusion models, fine-tuned on RECON, SCAND, TartanDrive (3-DoF navigation) and the 1X Humanoid dataset (25-DoF navigation and manipulation)
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB initial frame plus action sequence (plus initial joint state for humanoid)
setting.action_space: 3-DoF (dx, dy, dphi) navigation deltas; 25-DoF humanoid joint angles/gripper
setting.simulator: none (offline real-world datasets; generated video as the simulator)
setting.privileged: Planning uses a goal image; SCS uses manual point annotations (GT videos) for evaluation only; success on 1X is judged by humans

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjNav benchmarks; results are world-model prediction metrics (LPIPS/DreamSim/SCS) and planning ATE/SR. Only frame-16 rows are listed; other horizons and the 1X manipulation-planning SR table (Cosmos: 100/80/60/66.7%) are in the paper.
results: All EgoWM variants beat NWM on RECON at every horizon; at frame 16 SVD reaches SCS 55.2 vs NWM 33.4 (up to +65%). EgoWM also has roughly 6x faster 64-frame inference and about 8x less training compute than NWM. It scales to 25-DoF humanoids and generalizes to paintings, and planning ATE is slightly better than NWM (3.13 vs 3.25).
limitations: Small manipulated objects distort and object permanence fails; scenes sometimes collapse to the real-world distribution when generalizing to paintings.
Temporally compressed DiT variants (Cosmos, Wan) lose action-following at long horizons compared with SVD.
SCS main results rely on manual point annotation, and SCS ignores newly appearing content; manipulation planning success is judged by humans, with no simulator.
